files.name: 01-asakusa-sensoji-panorama.png
files.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset: ONE continuous exterior-only Tokyo panorama for the moving background OUTSIDE a train window. Supplied image is STYLE, PALETTE AND CAMERA-HEIGHT REFERENCE only, not an edit target. Invent a new district composition, do not repeat its clock building or river layout.
Format and camera: extra-wide horizontal 3:1 landscape, same dimensions/aspect as reference (2172x724 if possible). Calm level broadside view from a passing elevated train, distant-to-midrange scenery that can slide horizontally. Buildings and trees stay vertical. Avoid deep vanishing-point streets, aerial isometric views, wide-angle lens distortion or tilted horizon. Landmark silhouettes remain fully inside the frame with room above; quiet continuation of the district occupies both 10% side margins.
Match the reference's fine dark architectural outlines, richly painted yet crisp anime-background illustration, subtle paper texture, warm peach/coral sunset sky, sparse lavender clouds, muted lavender distant skyline, soft golden lit windows and spring cherry blossoms. Same golden-hour brightness across the series, no night or weather shift. Stable visual scale and clear foreground/middle/far depth cues. Exterior artwork fills the entire frame edge to edge.
ABSOLUTELY NO train interior, no window outline/frame/glass, no table, no TABI, no character portrait, no border, no panels/collage, no caption, no logos, no readable signage. Do not insert a train window merely because this art will be seen through one. Small incidental distant people optional, never the focal point. Opaque full landscape.
DISTRICT CONTENT: Asakusa temple district: the red Senso-ji temple hall and a slender five-storey pagoda seen broadside across a quiet low tiled boundary wall and old shop roofs. Temple complex offset from center, not a giant frontal gate filling the image. Several layered grey-blue tiled roofs, muted vermilion woodwork, small golden details, cherry trees and mature green trees around the complex. Quiet side streets and low traditional shops continue left and right; a few soft modern city silhouettes far behind. Use a LAND foreground of low rooftops/garden wall, NOT a canal, not a waterfront. Rich historic architecture and varied roof heights give a recognisably different exterior section.
files.review: Temple hall, pagoda and layered residential roofs over land; no interior or window border; golden-hour palette and level exterior framing.
